title: APC activation API (issuer for licensing method B, online-activation)
description: Request and response bodies of the issuer API v1. The plugin's only job is to POST these and hand the returned license to LicenseManager::activateFromText(), which re-verifies the signature locally - so the issuer, the transport and any proxy in between are untrusted. Any server can implement this (own WordPress/WooCommerce-style license plugin, hosted service, scripts/lib/license-issuer.js as the zero-dependency reference). Transport: JSON bodies, Content-Type: application/json on every POST, HTTPS in production. Routes: GET /v1/health; POST /v1/activate; POST /v1/deactivate; POST /v1/offline/request; POST /v1/offline/redeem. Error bodies use $defs/errorResponse; suggested HTTP status: 400 bad_request|product_mismatch|invalid_request_code, 403 invalid_serial|revoked, 409 seat_limit, 413 payload_too_large, 415 unsupported_media_type, 429 rate_limited, 404 not_found, 405 method_not_allowed, 500 server_error. Machine components are salted hashes only (never raw hardware identifiers).

machineComponents.description: machineFingerprint() of ApcLicense.h: salted 64-bit component hashes. The issuer identifies a machine k-of-n (same rule as the plugin), so one swapped disk or NIC is still the same seat.

serial.description: The license key the customer typed. The reference issuer uses 20 Crockford base32 characters in 4 groups of 5 (last character is a check character) and compares it in constant time against stored hashes; a WooCommerce-style plugin has its own key format - the plugin must not assume one.

email.description: Optional second factor: when present and the key has an email on record they must match (case-insensitive).

license.description: The signed apc-license/1.0 object. The plugin saves it (any whitespace; signing is over canonical JSON) and verifies it locally.

license_text.description: Optional convenience: the license pretty-printed, ready to write to license.lic or to offer as a download.

already_registered.description: true when this machine already held a seat (idempotent re-activation).

freed.description: false when this machine held no seat (idempotent: still ok).

requestCodePayload.description: Decoded content of the offline request code the plugin shows. The code itself is base64url (no padding) of this object as UTF-8 JSON.

request_code.description: base64url of requestCodePayload; surrounding whitespace/line breaks pasted by the customer are ignored.

offlineRequestResponse.description: Dry run for a confirmation page: validates the code and the key, consumes NO seat.

serial_hint.description: Masked key so the page can show which key is being registered.

error.description: Stable machine-readable code the plugin switches on. invalid_serial is returned for unknown keys AND for a wrong email, so the endpoint does not reveal which keys exist.

message.description: English text for logs / support; the plugin shows its own localised wording.
